claim: Terc constitutes a non-coding RNA critical for telomerase function.
source: The telomerase RNA component (Terc) constitutes a non-coding RNA critical for telomerase function, commonly associated with aging and pivotal in immunomodulation during inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a background fact about Terc.

claim: Terc is commonly associated with aging.
source: The telomerase RNA component (Terc) constitutes a non-coding RNA critical for telomerase function, commonly associated with aging and pivotal in immunomodulation during inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Terc is pivotal in immunomodulation during inflammation.
source: The telomerase RNA component (Terc) constitutes a non-coding RNA critical for telomerase function, commonly associated with aging and pivotal in immunomodulation during inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Tercko/ko mice show heightened susceptibility to pneumonia caused by Staphylococcus aureus compared to both young and old infected counterparts.
source: Our study unveils heightened susceptibility to pneumonia caused by Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) in Terc knockout (Tercko/ko) mice compared to both young and old infected counterparts.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: The exacerbated infection in Tercko/ko mice correlates with heightened inflammation.
source: The exacerbated infection in Tercko/ko mice correlates with heightened inflammation, manifested by elevated interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels and activation of the NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome within the lung.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by cytokine measurements and sequencing data.

claim: Tercko/ko mice show elevated interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels in the lung.
source: The exacerbated infection in Tercko/ko mice correlates with heightened inflammation, manifested by elevated interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels and activation of the NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome within the lung.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Tercko/ko mice show activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome within the lung.
source: The exacerbated infection in Tercko/ko mice correlates with heightened inflammation, manifested by elevated interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels and activation of the NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome within the lung.
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data showing upregulation of NLRP3 inflammasome pathway genes.

claim: Terc deletion results in compromised T cell function.
source: Terc deletion results in compromised T cell function, characterized by dysregulation of the T cell receptor and absence of CD247, potentially compromising the host's capacity to mount an effective immune response against S. aureus.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by sequencing data and flow cytometry experiments.

claim: Terc deletion is characterized by dysregulation of the T cell receptor.
source: Terc deletion results in compromised T cell function, characterized by dysregulation of the T cell receptor and absence of CD247, potentially compromising the host's capacity to mount an effective immune response against S. aureus.
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data showing downregulation of TCR signaling pathway genes.

claim: Terc deletion is characterized by absence of CD247.
source: Terc deletion results in compromised T cell function, characterized by dysregulation of the T cell receptor and absence of CD247, potentially compromising the host's capacity to mount an effective immune response against S. aureus.
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data and flow cytometry showing absence of CD247 expression in infected Tercko/ko mice.

claim: Advanced age (≥60 years) is among the most relevant risk factors leading to higher susceptibility to community-acquired and healthcare-associated pneumonia.
source: Among the most relevant risk factors leading to higher susceptibility as well as severity in both community-acquired (CA) and healthcare-associated (HA) pneumonia is advanced age (≥60 years) (Torres et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Torres et al., 2021.

claim: Advanced age (≥60 years) is among the most relevant risk factors leading to higher severity in both community-acquired and healthcare-associated pneumonia.
source: Among the most relevant risk factors leading to higher susceptibility as well as severity in both community-acquired (CA) and healthcare-associated (HA) pneumonia is advanced age (≥60 years) (Torres et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Torres et al., 2021.

claim: Pneumonia caused by Staphylococcus aureus is particularly severe.
source: Particularly severe is pneumonia caused by Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2022.

claim: S. aureus is a gram-positive bacterium that frequently colonizes humans.
source: S. aureus is a gram-positive bacterium that frequently colonizes humans but can manifest various pathologies, ranging from mild to more severe infections, including pneumonia (Howden et al., 2023; Jong et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Howden et al., 2023 and Jong et al., 2019.

claim: S. aureus can manifest various pathologies, ranging from mild to more severe infections, including pneumonia.
source: S. aureus is a gram-positive bacterium that frequently colonizes humans but can manifest various pathologies, ranging from mild to more severe infections, including pneumonia (Howden et al., 2023; Jong et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Howden et al., 2023 and Jong et al., 2019.

claim: S. aureus accounts for a notable proportion of community-acquired and healthcare-associated pneumonia cases.
source: It accounts for a notable proportion of CA and HA cases (Lee et al., 2022; Torres et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2022 and Torres et al., 2021.

claim: S. aureus exhibits a broad spectrum of virulence factors, including toxins, adhesins, and immune evasion strategies.
source: The bacterium exhibits a broad spectrum of virulence factors, including toxins, adhesins, and immune evasion strategies, contributing to its ability to establish infections in the lower respiratory tract (Howden et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Howden et al., 2023.

claim: Aging is a central factor predisposing individuals to a higher risk for S. aureus pneumonia.
source: Aging is a central factor predisposing individuals to a higher risk for S. aureus pneumonia (Torres et al., 2021), as aging is impacting several important functions of the body such as the immune response and thus the capability to mount an effective defensive response (Montecino-Rodriguez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Torres et al., 2021 and Montecino-Rodriguez et al., 2013.

claim: Aging impacts several important functions of the body such as the immune response and thus the capability to mount an effective defensive response.
source: Aging is a central factor predisposing individuals to a higher risk for S. aureus pneumonia (Torres et al., 2021), as aging is impacting several important functions of the body such as the immune response and thus the capability to mount an effective defensive response (Montecino-Rodriguez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Montecino-Rodriguez et al., 2013.

claim: Aging-related dysregulation of the immune response is characterized by inflammaging.
source: Aging-related dysregulation of the immune response is also characterized by inflammaging, defined as the presence of elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the absence of an obvious inflammatory trigger (Franceschi et al., 2000; Mogilenko et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Franceschi et al., 2000 and Mogilenko et al., 2022.

claim: Inflammaging is defined as the presence of elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the absence of an obvious inflammatory trigger.
source: Aging-related dysregulation of the immune response is also characterized by inflammaging, defined as the presence of elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the absence of an obvious inflammatory trigger (Franceschi et al., 2000; Mogilenko et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Franceschi et al., 2000 and Mogilenko et al., 2022.

claim: Immune cells, such as macrophages, exhibit an activated state that alters their response to infection during aging.
source: Additionally, immune cells, such as macrophages, exhibit an activated state that alters their response to infection (Canan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Canan et al., 2014.

claim: The immune response of macrophages to infectious challenges has been shown to be initially impaired in aged mice.
source: In contrast, the immune response of macrophages to infectious challenges has been shown to be initially impaired in aged mice (Boe et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Boe et al., 2017.

claim: Telomere shortening is a significant factor in cellular aging.
source: Among these hallmarks, telomere shortening is a significant factor in cellular aging.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about aging hallmarks.

claim: Telomeres serve as protective caps at the end of chromosomes, which shorten with every cell division until they reach a critical length where replication becomes impossible, eventually resulting in either apoptosis or senescence.
source: Telomeres serve as protective caps at the end of chromosomes, which shorten with every cell division until they reach a critical length where replication becomes impossible, eventually resulting in either apoptosis or senescence (López-Otín et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to López-Otín et al., 2023.

claim: Telomerase can add new repeats to the ends of chromosomes and thus prevent the shortening of telomeres.
source: However, this process can be counteracted by the telomerase, which can add new repeats to the ends of chromosomes and thus prevent the shortening of telomeres (Greider and Blackburn, 1985).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Greider and Blackburn, 1985.

claim: The telomerase mainly consists of two parts: the telomerase reverse transcriptase (Tert), which harbors the enzymatic activity, and Terc, which serves as a template for the addition of new repeats.
source: The telomerase mainly consists of two parts: the telomerase reverse transcriptase (Tert), which harbors the enzymatic activity, and Terc, which serves as a template for the addition of new repeats (Sahin and Depinho, 2010; Shay and Wright, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sahin and Depinho, 2010 and Shay and Wright, 2019.

claim: Telomerase activity is restricted to specific tissues and cell types, largely dependent on the expression of Tert.
source: Telomerase activity is restricted to specific tissues and cell types, largely dependent on the expression of Tert.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about telomerase.

claim: Tert is highly expressed in stem cells, progenitor cells, and germline cells.
source: While Tert is highly expressed in stem cells, progenitor cells, and germline cells, its expression is minimal in most differentiated cells (Chakravarti et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chakravarti et al., 2021.

claim: Tert expression is minimal in most differentiated cells.
source: While Tert is highly expressed in stem cells, progenitor cells, and germline cells, its expression is minimal in most differentiated cells (Chakravarti et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chakravarti et al., 2021.

claim: The impact of telomerase dysfunction on tissues varies according to their self-renewal rate.
source: Consequently, the impact of telomerase dysfunction on tissues varies according to their self-renewal rate (Chakravarti et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chakravarti et al., 2021.

claim: Tissues or organ systems that are highly replicative, such as the skin or the hematopoietic system, are affected first by telomere shortening.
source: Tissues or organ systems that are highly replicative, such as the skin or the hematopoietic system, are affected first by telomere shortening (Chakravarti et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chakravarti et al., 2021.

claim: While most differentiated cells do not exhibit telomerase activity, T cells display a high activity of this enzyme.
source: Interestingly, while most differentiated cells do not exhibit telomerase activity, T cells display a high activity of this enzyme (Hodes et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hodes et al., 2002.

claim: Aging T cells become senescent, which is characterized by short telomeres and the absence of CD28 expression.
source: Aging T cells become senescent, which is characterized by short telomeres and the absence of CD28 expression (Hohensinner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hohensinner et al., 2011.

claim: T cells with shorter telomeres are implicated in diseases related to aging like arthritis.
source: Furthermore, telomere length and T cell functionality are closely connected. T cells with shorter telomeres are implicated in diseases related to aging like arthritis (Hohensinner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hohensinner et al., 2011.

claim: CD4+ T cells from Terc knockout mice displayed several characteristics of aged T cells such as a reduction in CD28 expression and changed secretion of cytokines.
source: Additionally, CD4+ T cells from Terc knockout (Tercko/ko) mice displayed several characteristics of aged T cells such as a reduction in CD28 expression and changed secretion of cytokines. Furthermore the naïve T cell population was found to be reduced (Matthe et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Matthe et al., 2022.

claim: The naïve T cell population was found to be reduced in CD4+ T cells from Terc knockout mice.
source: Additionally, CD4+ T cells from Terc knockout (Tercko/ko) mice displayed several characteristics of aged T cells such as a reduction in CD28 expression and changed secretion of cytokines. Furthermore the naïve T cell population was found to be reduced (Matthe et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Matthe et al., 2022.

claim: Almost all human cells and several murine tissues express Terc.
source: While most differentiated cells lack the expression of Tert, almost all human cells and several murine tissues express Terc (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Terc triggers inflammation via the nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) pathway.
source: Notably, a study could show that Terc triggers inflammation via the nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) pathway (Liu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2019.

claim: Terc was identified to be involved in cell proliferation by enhancing the expression of several genes belonging to the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (Pi3K)-protein kinase B (AKT) pathway.
source: Furthermore, Terc was identified to be involved in cell proliferation by enhancing the expression of several genes belonging to the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (Pi3K)-protein kinase B (AKT) pathway (Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wu et al., 2022.

claim: Terc contributes to CD4+ T cell expansion.
source: The same study could show that this mechanism also contributed to CD4+ T cell expansion (Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wu et al., 2022.

claim: Terc deletion in mice induced NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages upon pulmonary infection with S. aureus.
source: Additionally, Terc deletion in mice induced NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation in macrophages upon pulmonary infection with S. aureus, thereby revealing another connection between immune modulation and the presence of Terc (Kang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kang et al., 2018.

claim: Downregulation of Terc and Tert expression in tissues of aged mice and rats has been found.
source: Interestingly, downregulation of Terc and Tert expression in tissues of aged mice and rats has been found (Tarry-Adkins et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tarry-Adkins et al., 2021 and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Knockout of Terc in mice is a well-established model for premature aging.
source: Knockout of Terc in mice is a well-established model for premature aging, as telomeres of Tercko/ko mice shorten with every generation (Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wong et al., 2009.

claim: Telomeres of Tercko/ko mice shorten with every generation.
source: Knockout of Terc in mice is a well-established model for premature aging, as telomeres of Tercko/ko mice shorten with every generation (Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wong et al., 2009.

claim: The telomeres shorten during each generation with increasing age of the Tercko/ko mice.
source: Additionally, the telomeres shorten during each generation with increasing age of the mice (Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wong et al., 2009.

claim: Third-generation (G3) Tercko/ko mice with a C56Bl/6 background have a shorter lifespan.
source: Furthermore, third-generation (G3) Tercko/ko mice with a C56Bl/6 background have a shorter lifespan, a smaller litter size, and a generally reduced body size and weight (Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wong et al., 2009.

claim: Third-generation (G3) Tercko/ko mice with a C56Bl/6 background have a smaller litter size.
source: Furthermore, third-generation (G3) Tercko/ko mice with a C56Bl/6 background have a shorter lifespan, a smaller litter size, and a generally reduced body size and weight (Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wong et al., 2009.

claim: Third-generation (G3) Tercko/ko mice with a C56Bl/6 background have a generally reduced body size and weight.
source: Furthermore, third-generation (G3) Tercko/ko mice with a C56Bl/6 background have a shorter lifespan, a smaller litter size, and a generally reduced body size and weight (Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wong et al., 2009.

claim: The clinical score of infected Tercko/ko mice was increased compared to the other two infected mice cohorts at 24 hr post infection.
source: The clinical score of infected Tercko/ko mice was increased compared to the other two infected mice cohorts at 24 hr post infection (hpi) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The bacterial load was significantly higher in the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) of Tercko/ko mice compared to old WT mice.
source: The bacterial load was significantly higher in the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) of Tercko/ko mice compared to old WT mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Three distinct degrees of severity were observed in the infected Tercko/ko mice: mild infection, systemic infections, or fatal infections.
source: Interestingly, three distinct degrees of severity were observed in the infected Tercko/ko mice (n=5): mild infection, systemic infections, or fatal infections (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Mice exhibiting systemic infection were characterized by the presence of bacteria in extrapulmonary organs, specifically observed in the liver and kidney tissues of some Tercko/ko mice.
source: Mice exhibiting systemic infection were characterized by the presence of bacteria in extrapulmonary organs, specifically observed in the liver and kidney tissues of some Tercko/ko mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Infection of young WT mice resulted in a significant decrease in body weight at 24 hpi.
source: Infection of young WT mice resulted in a significant decrease in body weight at 24 hpi.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The body weight of infected Tercko/ko mice was reduced compared to the infected old WT mice and the non-infected Tercko/ko mice.
source: The body weight of infected Tercko/ko mice was reduced compared to the infected old WT mice and the non-infected Tercko/ko mice (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: At 24 hpi the relative weight of the lung was increased in infected compared to the non-infected mice for all cohorts, indicating inflammation of the lung.
source: In contrast, at 24 hpi the relative weight of the lung was increased in infected compared to the non-infected mice for all cohorts, indicating inflammation of the lung (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D and interpreted as indicating inflammation.

claim: The telomeres of Tercko/ko mice were the shortest among the three different mouse models, even shorter than those of naturally aged mice.
source: Notably, the telomeres of Tercko/ko mice were the shortest among the three different mouse models, even shorter than those of naturally aged mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by telomere length measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Several pro-inflammatory cytokines were significantly upregulated in Tercko/ko mice with systemic infection, such as interleukin-6 (IL-6), granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, and interleukin-1β (IL-1β).
source: Several pro-inflammatory cytokines were significantly upregulated in Tercko/ko mice with systemic infection, such as interleukin-6 (IL-6), granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, and interleukin-1β (IL-1β).
evidence: This is supported by cytokine measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Other important pro-inflammatory factors like tumor necrosis factor α (TNFα) and interleukin-1α (IL-1α) were also elevated in Tercko/ko mice with systemic infection.
source: Other important pro-inflammatory factors like tumor necrosis factor α (TNFα) and interleukin-1α (IL-1α) were also elevated (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by cytokine measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A significant upregulation of pro-inflammatory mediators due to infection was solely detected in infected Tercko/ko mice compared to the corresponding non-infected control cohort.
source: A significant upregulation of pro-inflammatory mediators due to infection was, however, solely detected in infected Tercko/ko mice compared to the corresponding non-infected control cohort (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by cytokine measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Several genes related to the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, such as NLRP3 or thioredoxin interacting protein (TXNIP), were upregulated in infected Tercko/ko, indicating activation of the inflammasome.
source: Intriguingly, several genes related to the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, such as NLRP3 or thioredoxin interacting protein (TXNIP), were upregulated in infected Tercko/ko, indicating activation of the inflammasome (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Expression of genes encoding for TNFα, IL-1β, and IL-6 were heightened in infected Tercko/ko mice.
source: Notably, expression of genes encoding for TNFα, IL-1β, and IL-6 were heightened.
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The increased inflammation in the lungs of Tercko/ko mice is likely induced by activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: Thus, the increased inflammation in the lungs of Tercko/ko mice is likely induced by activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the sequencing data showing upregulation of NLRP3 inflammasome pathway genes.

claim: The nucleotide oligomerization domain-like receptor signaling pathway was among the most significantly enriched pathways when comparing infected Tercko/ko and young WT mice.
source: Supporting this, the nucleotide oligomerization domain-like receptor signaling pathway was among the most significantly enriched pathways when comparing infected Tercko/ko and young WT mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) are present in the lung and can directly react to the pathogen at the site of infection via the production of inflammatory mediators or attraction of other immune cells.
source: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) are present in the lung and can directly react to the pathogen at the site of infection via the production of inflammatory mediators or attraction of other immune cells (Malainou et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Malainou et al., 2023.

claim: AMs can phagocytose S. aureus.
source: By using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) we could strikingly visualize the ability of AMs to phagocytose S. aureus (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by SEM images shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage markers, such as C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2(CXCL2), were upregulated in Tercko/ko mice following infection.
source: Notably, our sequencing data revealed an upregulation of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage markers, such as C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2(CXCL2), in Tercko/ko mice following infection (Figure 3B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Anti-inflammatory M2 markers, e.g., interferon regulatory factor 4 (IRF4), were mainly downregulated in infected Tercko/ko mice.
source: Anti-inflammatory M2 markers, e.g., interferon regulatory factor 4 (IRF4), were mainly downregulated.
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Cluster of differentiation 14 (CD14), a general macrophage marker, was increased in the infected Tercko/ko mice.
source: Additionally, cluster of differentiation 14 (CD14), a general macrophage marker, was increased in the infected Tercko/ko mice (Figure 3B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The expression of multiple chemokines such as C-X-C motif ligand 1–3 (CXCL1-3) and C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) was elevated in infected Tercko/ko mice, suggesting increased migration of leukocytes such as macrophages and neutrophils to the lung.
source: Furthermore, the expression of multiple chemokines such as C-X-C motif ligand 1–3 (CXCL1-3) and C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) was elevated, suggesting increased migration of leukocytes such as macrophages and neutrophils to the lung (Figure 3C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, with interpretation about leukocyte migration.

claim: The TNF, NF-κB, and IL-17 signaling pathways were among the most significantly enriched pathways in infected Tercko/ko mice compared to young WT mice.
source: Additionally, the TNF, NF-κB, and IL-17 signaling pathways were among the most significantly enriched pathways in infected Tercko/ko mice compared to young WT mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Multiple general T cell markers such as CD2, CD5, and CD4 were downregulated in the infected Tercko/ko mice compared to young WT mice.
source: Surprisingly, multiple general T cell markers such as CD2, CD5, and CD4 were downregulated in the infected Tercko/ko mice compared to young WT mice (Figure 4A; Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: These distinctions in T cell markers are not evident in comparisons between non-infected Tercko/ko and young WT mice.
source: However, these distinctions are not evident in comparisons between non-infected Tercko/ko and young WT mice.
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The observed variations in immune response activation arise specifically in response to infection.
source: This further emphasizes that the observed variations in immune response activation arise specifically in response to infection (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the comparison of infected and non-infected mice.

claim: Some T cell markers, such as CD5, that were downregulated in infected Tercko/ko mice were also downregulated in infected old WT mice compared to young WT mice.
source: Some T cell markers, such as CD5, that were downregulated in infected Tercko/ko mice were also downregulated in infected old WT mice compared to young WT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: No significant difference in CD3+ T cell percentage was observed between young WT, old WT, and Tercko/ko mice spleen.
source: However, no significant difference was observed between the groups (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Several genes belonging to the T cell receptor (TCR) signaling pathway were downregulated in infected Tercko/ko mice, such as CD3G (encoding CD3γ) and CD247 encoding CD3ζ.
source: Additionally, several genes belonging to the T cell receptor (TCR) signaling pathway were downregulated in infected Tercko/ko mice, such as CD3G (encoding CD3γ) and CD247 encoding CD3ζ (Figure 4C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Expression of downstream factors of the TCR like lymphocyte cell-specific protein-tyrosine kinase (LCK), linker of activation (LAT), and IL-2 inducible T cell kinase (ITK) was reduced in infected Tercko/ko mice.
source: Expression of downstream factors of the TCR like lymphocyte cell-specific protein-tyrosine kinase (LCK), linker of activation (LAT), and IL-2 inducible T cell kinase (ITK) was also reduced (Figure 4C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: CD247 was the only gene downregulated compared to infected young WT, old WT, and non-infected Tercko/ko mice.
source: Specifically, CD247 was the only gene downregulated compared to infected young WT, old WT, and non-infected Tercko/ko mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CD247 was downregulated in infected old WT mice compared to infected young WT mice.
source: Additionally, CD247 was downregulated in infected old WT mice compared to infected young WT mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CD247 is an essential factor for the assembly of the TCR and the downstream signaling after stimulation with an antigen.
source: CD247 is an essential factor for the assembly of the TCR and the downstream signaling after stimulation with an antigen (Jin et al., 2024; Pitcher et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jin et al., 2024 and Pitcher et al., 2003.

claim: In young WT mice gene expression levels of CD247 were increased with infection, likely due to proliferation and infiltration of T cells.
source: In young WT mice gene expression levels of CD247 were increased with infection, likely due to proliferation and infiltration of T cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4D, with interpretation about T cell proliferation and infiltration.

claim: In infected Tercko/ko mice, the expression of CD247 is absent.
source: Notably, in infected Tercko/ko mice, the expression of CD247 is absent.
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There is no difference in CD247 expression between non-infected and infected old WT mice.
source: Moreover, there is no difference in CD247 expression between non-infected and infected old WT mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The TCR signaling pathway and Th1 and Th2 differentiation pathway are among the most enriched pathways in infected young WT mice compared to non-infected young WT mice.
source: Additionally, the TCR signaling pathway and Th1 and Th2 differentiation pathway are among the most enriched pathways in infected young WT mice compared to non-infected young WT mice.
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The TCR signaling pathway and Th1 and Th2 differentiation pathway are not upregulated when comparing infected Tercko/ko with non-infected Tercko/ko mice.
source: In contrast, those pathways are not upregulated when comparing infected Tercko/ko with non-infected Tercko/ko mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: AMs of Tercko/ko and young WT mice successfully internalized S. aureus.
source: IF staining of AMs of Tercko/ko and young WT mice revealed the successful internalization of S. aureus as well as a change of phenotypic appearance to a more activated shape (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 5C.

claim: AMs of Tercko/ko and young WT mice showed a change of phenotypic appearance to a more activated shape after S. aureus infection.
source: IF staining of AMs of Tercko/ko and young WT mice revealed the successful internalization of S. aureus as well as a change of phenotypic appearance to a more activated shape (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 5C.

claim: There was a substantial elevation in the baseline expression of CD247 in T cells from Tercko/ko mice in comparison to T cells from young WT mice at 24 hpi.
source: Utilizing flow cytometry, we observed a substantial elevation in the baseline expression of CD247 in T cells from Tercko/ko mice in comparison to T cells from young WT mice at 24 hpi (Figure 5D).
